chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with the one in Ihram changing his clothes. But, when he enters Makkah, he should wear the two garments of his Ihram in which he entered the state of Ihram, and it is disliked that he sells them.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What are the rules regarding the Ihram garments when entering Makkah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the practical jurisprudence of Ihram, distinguishing between the general permissibility of changing garments and the specific ritual requirement to don the original two pieces upon entering the sacred precincts of Makkah. The prohibition against selling these garments underscores their symbolic value as a continuous link to the state of consecration, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving the integrity of ritual symbols throughout the pilgrimage journey.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There is no problem with the one in Ihraam changing his clothes. But, when he enters Makkah, he should wear two (pieces of) clothes which he has worn Ihraam in, and it is disliked that he sells these two’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
if one in the state of Ihram can wear al-Khazz (fur of a certain animal that lives in water). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful . ‘“
